thread:
Maya (support): Escalation from customer NimbusPay. They hit a 400 with "json_schema_error" when calling our function/tool API. Customer pasted the exact error below.

```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": {
    "type": "json_schema_error",
    "message": "additionalProperties <<'cache'>> not allowed",
    "details": [
      { "path": "/tools/download_file", "issue": "required property 'method' missing" },
      { "path": "/tools/download_file/params/timeout", "issue": "expected integer, got string" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Maya (support): They say their payload is: 

```
{
  "tool": "download_file",
  "params": {
    "url": "https://api.nimbus.example/download/123",
    "cache": true,
    "timeout": "45s"
  }
}
```

Maya (support): They migrated from an older SDK and claim the server used to accept "cache" and string timeouts. Now the function-caller layer rejects it. Customer asks for a repro + a mitigation ASAP (affecting production). :alarm_clock:

support-bot: Ticket #4678 created and escalated to @eng. SLA timer started.

Theo (eng): @Maya can you get the request_id and SDK version? we need the exact request to correlate with logs.

Maya (support): Customer returned request_id=np-20260402-2210, SDK=redwood-js v0.9.2.

Ravi (sre): Pulled logs for np-20260402-2210. Schema validation fails in pre-routing validator. Raw inbound: additional property "cache" + timeout as string. Stack trace: func-caller -> json-schema-validator v2 -> edge-proxy. I'll redact and paste the key lines.

Theo (eng): Paste logs, please. My preliminary check: our canonical schema for download_file params is { url: string, method: string (required), timeout: integer (ms) } with additionalProperties: false. The client omitted method and added cache and a string timeout. Looks like an SDK serialization mismatch.

Ravi (sre): Logs: 

```
[2026-04-02T08:21:47Z] np-20260402-2210 inbound: {"tool":"download_file","params":{"url":"https://api.nimbus.example/download/123","cache":true,"timeout":"45s"}}
[2026-04-02T08:21:47Z] json-schema-validator: validation failed for /tools/download_file: additionalProperties: ["cache"] not allowed; missing required: ["method"]; type mismatch at params.timeout: expected integer
[2026-04-02T08:21:47Z] edge-proxy: returned 400 for np-20260402-2210
```

Theo (eng): Confirmed. Root cause: mismatch between legacy client payloads and our strict function-calling JSON Schema. Options: (A) tell customer to change payload to include "method": "GET", convert timeout to ms integer (45000), and drop "cache"; (B) add server-side compatibility shim to coerce/clean known legacy shapes.

Maya (support): Customer asked if we can do server-side compat immediately since they have many services. Any chance we can enable a tenant-scoped shim? They need traffic unblocked within hours.

Theo (eng): Short-term we can add a small middleware in function-caller: pre-validate normalizer that will (1) convert timeout strings like "45s" or "45000" to integer ms; (2) default missing "method" to "GET"; (3) drop deprecated keys ("cache") based on a blacklist. We'll gate behind a per-tenant feature flag and emit a compat metric. I'll own the implementation and tests. Low-risk but needs code review.

Ravi (sre): If we enable coercion we must log all coerced requests and bump a metric so we can roll back if unexpected. Also watch latency impact; doing extra parsing is small but worth monitoring. Recommend canary 5-10% first.

Maya (support): Customer is OK with an opt-in shim for their tenant only. They replied "PLEASE ENABLE".

support-bot: Feature flag `legacy_tool_payload_compat_v1` enabled for tenant nimbus-987 (canary=10%).

Theo (eng): Drafting PR: https://git.internal/redwood/function-caller/pull/2137. Change summary: add pre-validation middleware normalizer + unit tests; per-tenant feature flag; add metric `tool_compat_applied` and log field `compat_applied:true`. Will request @Ravi review and then merge behind the flag. ETA ~2.5h for initial canary.

Ravi (sre): Monitoring dashboards: added alert for schema-validator error rate for download_file and a panel for `tool_compat_applied`. We'll keep watch for anomalous spikes/errors and any increased 5xxs.

Maya (support): Sending a short note to Nimbus: 

```
Hi Nimbus team,

We can enable a backward-compatibility shim for your tenant that will: 1) coerce string timeouts like "45s" to integer ms; 2) assume missing "method" is "GET"; 3) ignore deprecated "cache" param. This is opt-in and reversible. We will roll it out as a 10% canary first and monitor for regressions. Reply CONFIRM to proceed and we will enable it and monitor.
```

Maya (support): Nimbus replied CONFIRM. :white_check_mark:

Theo (eng): After canary, if metrics look good we'll promote to 100%. Also plan a follow-up: coordinate with SDK team to release a patch (redwood-js v0.9.4) that serializes timeout as integer and drops cache param. We'll include a migration note in the changelog.

Maya (support): Thanks team, I'll update Nimbus and close the loop once the canary succeeds.

support-bot: Ticket #4678 status updated: compat enabled (canary=10%).
